- Replace the strip-shaped level with a spacious, explorable 3D isometric fantasy kingdom while preserving core gameplay.
- Finish the redesign and verify it in Preview.

## Requirements
- Build a continuous landscape with varied terrain, connected biomes, rivers, bridges, paths, villages, ruins, castles, caves, and hidden locations.
- Support free exploration, suitable collision/navigation, and Android performance.
- Preserve working movement, joystick, animation, combat, and UI while keeping the angled orthographic isometric camera; avoid linear arenas and endless-runner layouts.

## Decisions
- Retain the existing logical 2D gameplay coordinates projected into 3D; adapt map and region data rather than rewrite gameplay wholesale.
- Arrange five biomes across a broad map, connected by winding paths and river crossings.
- Keep existing controls, combat, and UI while replacing terrain and level layout.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the map and distributed five biome locations in `game.js`.
- Added procedural terrain height, nearest-region lookup using `(x, y)`, path-distance calculation, blended biome ground colors, and river/bridge helper functions.
- Replaced strip ground/trail generation with broad terrain, winding path ribbons, a river, bridges, village, shrine/keep landmarks, and cave geometry.
- Reworked ground cover and tree/rock placement to use biome locations, terrain height, paths, and river distances.

### Active
- Adapt gameplay placement and terrain alignment for actors, objects, gates, checkpoints, and coins.
- Replace strip-era reset, progression, and win logic with behavior suited to five dispersed biomes; pass both coordinates to every `regionAt` call.

- (none)

## Objective
- Replace the strip-shaped level with a spacious, explorable 3D isometric fantasy kingdom while preserving core gameplay.
- Finish the redesign and verify it in Preview.

## Requirements
- Create connected biomes with varied terrain, rivers, bridges, paths, villages, ruins, castles, caves, and hidden locations.
- Support free exploration and suitable collision/navigation, with Android performance in mind.
- Preserve movement, controls, animation, combat, UI, and the angled orthographic camera; avoid linear arenas and endless-runner layouts.

## Decisions
- Retain the existing logical 2D gameplay coordinates projected into 3D.
- Arrange five biomes across a broad map, connected by paths and river crossings.
- Keep existing controls, combat, and UI while adapting the world and progression.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the map with five dispersed biome locations, terrain, paths, river, landmarks, and biome-aware vegetation.
- Updated reset and progression objects, region lookup, and bridge/river collision.
- Fixed terrain elevation positioning for the hero, enemies, and bosses.
- Updated the win condition to require reaching the final gate after collecting all keys.
- `node --check game.js` passed; Preview opened, gameplay started, and navigation was tested.
- Refreshed `screenshots/natural-world-preview.png`; no JavaScript console errors were reported.

- Inspect the refreshed screenshot and confirm the Preview appearance meets the redesign goals.

- (none)

3. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and Preview checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World generation, collision, gameplay objects, combat, and progression.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `screenshots/natural-world-preview.png`: Refreshed Preview screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the latest `git status`.
- Runtime Preview is available at `http://localhost:3002`.

## Objective
- Replace the strip-shaped level with a spacious, explorable 3D isometric fantasy kingdom while preserving core gameplay.
- Finish the redesign and verify it in Preview.

## Requirements
- Create connected biomes with varied terrain, rivers, bridges, paths, villages, ruins, castles, caves, and hidden locations.
- Support free exploration and suitable collision/navigation, with Android performance in mind.
- Preserve movement, controls, animation, combat, UI, and the angled orthographic camera; avoid linear arenas and endless-runner layouts.

## Decisions
- Retain the existing logical 2D gameplay coordinates projected into 3D.
- Arrange five biomes across a broad map, connected by paths and river crossings.
- Keep existing controls, combat, and UI while adapting the world and progression.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the map with five dispersed biome locations, terrain, paths, river, landmarks, and biome-aware vegetation.

- Updated the win condition to require reaching the final gate after collecting all keys.
- `node --check game.js` passed; Preview opened and showed the game with no JavaScript console errors.
- Refreshed `screenshots/natural-world-preview.png`; tested movement and restart/attack input in Preview.

### Active
- Verify navigation and progression across biomes, including boss and gate interactions and bridge alignment.
- Inspect the refreshed screenshot and confirm the Preview appearance meets the redesign goals.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/natural-world-preview.png` and assess map appearance and framing.
2. Continue testing movement, combat, bridges, and boss/key/gate progression across dispersed regions.
3. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and Preview checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World generation, collision, gameplay objects, combat, and progression.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `screenshots/natural-world-preview.png`: Refreshed Preview screenshot.

## Objective
- Fix player collision and movement so the hero slides smoothly around solid scenery without getting trapped, while preserving the game’s controls and design.

## Requirements
- Reliable collisions with trees, rocks, stones, and other solid objects; no walking through them.
- Smooth eight-direction movement and sliding, open spaces between obstacles, suitable object-sized boundaries, and safe recovery if stuck.
- Test dense tree groups, rocks, narrow paths, and village buildings.
- Preserve the joystick, camera, character, and world design.

## Decisions
- Use smaller trunk-based tree colliders while leaving canopies walk-through.
- Size rock colliders to their geometry and space new rocks away from existing obstacles.
- Use incremental movement with axis sliding, tangential movement around rounded corners, and a last-safe-position recovery.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added village hut collision and adjusted tree and rock collision radii and placement spacing.
- Reworked `moveWithCollision` for small movement steps, sliding, tangent projection, and recovery from blocked positions.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Validate collision behavior around dense scenery, narrow paths, and village buildings; refine if testing reveals issues.

- (none)

1. Test the game’s collision and movement behavior in Preview, including recovery from a trapped position.
2. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Objective
- Fix player collision and movement so the hero slides smoothly around solid scenery without getting trapped, while preserving the game’s controls and design.

## Requirements
- Reliable collisions with trees, rocks, stones, and other solid objects; no walking through them.
- Smooth eight-direction movement and sliding, open spaces between obstacles, suitable object-sized boundaries, and safe recovery if stuck.
- Test dense tree groups, rocks, narrow paths, and village buildings.
- Preserve the joystick, camera, character, and world design.

## Decisions
- Use smaller trunk-based tree colliders while leaving canopies walk-through.
- Size rock colliders to their geometry and space new rocks away from existing obstacles.
- Use incremental movement with axis sliding, tangential movement around rounded corners, and a last-safe-position recovery.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added village hut collision and adjusted tree and rock collision radii and placement spacing.
- Reworked `moveWithCollision` for small movement steps, sliding, tangent projection, and recovery from blocked positions.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Opened the game in Playwright at `http://localhost:3002/`; page loaded with zero console errors.

### Active
- Validate collision behavior around dense scenery, narrow paths, and village buildings, including recovery from a trapped position.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test movement and collision behavior in the open browser, including dense obstacles, narrow paths, village buildings, and recovery.
2. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World object colliders, collision checks, and player/enemy movement.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- Movement behavior has not yet been tested in the browser; current browser verification only confirmed the page loads without console errors.

## Objective
- Fix player collision and movement so the hero slides smoothly around solid scenery without getting trapped, while preserving the game’s controls and design.

## Requirements
- Reliable collisions with trees, rocks, stones, and other solid objects; no walking through them.
- Smooth eight-direction movement and sliding, open spaces between obstacles, suitable object-sized boundaries, and safe recovery if stuck.
- Test dense tree groups, rocks, narrow paths, and village buildings.
- Preserve the joystick, camera, character, and world design.

## Decisions
- Use smaller trunk-based tree colliders while leaving canopies walk-through.
- Size rock colliders to their geometry and space new rocks away from existing obstacles.
- Use incremental movement with axis sliding, tangential movement around rounded corners, and a last-safe-position recovery.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added village hut collision and adjusted tree and rock collision radii and placement spacing.
- Reworked `moveWithCollision` for small movement steps, sliding, tangent projection, and recovery from blocked positions.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Opened `http://localhost:3002/`; page loaded with zero console errors. Browser is at the introductory screen.

### Active
- Validate collision behavior around dense scenery, narrow paths, and village buildings, including recovery from a trapped position.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Begin the quest in the browser and test movement and collision behavior around dense obstacles, narrow paths, village buildings, and a trapped position.
2. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World object colliders, collision checks, and player/enemy movement.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in `git status --short`.
- `http://localhost:3002/` was already serving the game; an attempted second Python server failed because the address was in use.
- Browser reported zero errors and four warnings on the latest snapshot; collision behavior has not yet been tested.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

- Trees should gently sway in the wind.
- Branches and leaves should have subtle natural movement.
- Bushes and plants should move slightly with the wind.

2. GRASS:

- Grass should sway naturally.

- Rivers should visibly flow.
- Waterfalls should have continuous flowing animation.
- Lakes and ponds should have subtle animated ripples.
- Add realistic water reflections where performance allows.

4. ENVIRONMENTAL ATMOSPHERE:

- Add floating dust particles and occasional fireflies.
- Add gentle atmospheric mist in suitable areas.
- Add subtle environmental lighting effects.

5. SKY AND LIGHTING:

- Add slowly moving clouds if the existing sky system supports them.
- Improve natural sunlight and dynamic shadows where practical.

6. ENVIRONMENTAL DETAILS:

- Add subtle movement to suitable environmental objects.
- Make the world feel alive without excessive or distracting animations.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

- Use real-time animation in the existing Three.js environment.
- Keep animations smooth and continuous.
- Optimize all effects for Android devices.
- Avoid excessive draw calls and expensive effects.
- Use delta time for frame-rate-independent animation.
- Preserve the existing landscape, world layout, player, controls and camera.

- **Vegetation and rocks:** `buildGroundCover()` at [`game.js:297–332`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ) creates instanced meshes for 1,800 grass blades, 300 flowers, and 520 shrubs. `placeCover()` distributes them deterministically by biome and avoids trails, the river, and the central village. `buildTreesAndRocks()` at [`game.js:334–431`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ) uses instanced trunks and canopy/conifer layers for trees, plus 145 instanced rocks; tree and rock positions also populate `colliders`.

- Improve environmental animation throughout the existing Three.js game world while preserving the player, controls, camera, landscape, and world layout.
- Verify the implemented effects in Preview and report which are working.

## Requirements
- Animate trees, vegetation, and grass with subtle, varied wind movement; do not change main-character animations.

- Add floating dust, occasional fireflies, suitable mist, subtle environmental lighting, and slowly moving clouds if supported.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing Three.js update loop and reuse instancing or particle infrastructure where practical.
- Inspection found a river but no existing lakes or waterfalls; avoid inventing assets that would alter the world layout.

- Inspected environment assets and identified animation hooks: instanced trees/ground cover, static river ribbons, point-particle infrastructure, lighting/fog, and `update(dt)`/render loop.

- Implement environmental animations in `game.js` and verify their visible behavior in Preview.

- (none)

1. Add subtle, varied wind motion for instanced trees and ground cover, plus animated river flow and lightweight atmospheric particles/mist or lighting effects.
2. Keep effects delta-time-based and mindful of Android performance; preserve existing layout and gameplay.
3. Test in Preview, check console, and report which environmental animations are actually working.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene construction, vegetation, river, lighting/fog, particles, update loop, and renderer.

- `buildRiver()` creates static river ribbons; no lake or waterfall implementation was found.
- `buildGroundCover()` creates 1,800 grass blades, 300 flowers, and 520 shrubs with instanced meshes.

- Add gentle, varied wind motion to trees, vegetation, and grass without changing the main character’s animations.
- Animate river flow and add subtle water effects only where existing water supports them; do not add lakes or waterfalls.

- No lakes or waterfalls were found in the existing world.

I want a major upgrade to the visual quality and environmental presentation of my existing 3D fantasy RPG.

VISUAL REFERENCE: Zoria: Age of Shattering.


I want the world to have a similar level of environmental richness, depth, atmosphere and visual polish. Do not simply add a few moving trees or floating particles.


IMPORTANT: I want to upgrade the ENTIRE ENVIRONMENT, not the main character.


1. World visual quality


- Replace the generic, idle-game-looking appearance with a professionally designed fantasy RPG environment.
- Create detailed, natural-looking forests with varied tree shapes, dense vegetation and layered scenery.
- Improve terrain geometry, hills, cliffs, mountains and valleys.
- Add detailed rocks, roots, plants, shrubs and environmental decorations.
- Create beautiful distant scenery and atmospheric depth.


2. Advanced environmental animation


- Natural wind affecting trees, branches, leaves, grass and bushes.
- Realistic flowing rivers, waterfalls and animated water surfaces.
- Dynamic environmental effects such as drifting fog, dust, falling leaves and fireflies.
- Animated environmental objects where appropriate.
- Subtle environmental changes that make the world feel alive.


3. Lighting and atmosphere


- Improve lighting, shadows, ambient occlusion and material quality.
- Add realistic sunlight and atmospheric fog.
- Create beautiful lighting through forest trees.
- Improve environmental colour grading and depth.
- Make forests, caves, villages and ruins feel visually distinct.


4. Environmental detail


- Avoid repetitive tree and rock arrangements.
- Use varied terrain materials and natural transitions.
- Add small details that reward exploration.
- Make distant landmarks visually impressive.


5. Technical requirements


- Use advanced Three.js techniques supported by the existing project.
- Use suitable geometry, materials, shaders and animation systems.
- Optimize performance for Android devices.
- Avoid excessive particle effects and unnecessary shadows.
- Preserve the current world layout, player, controls, collision system and genuine 3D isometric camera.


VERY IMPORTANT


First inspect the current rendering system and explain honestly what visual improvements are technically possible.


Do not pretend that simple procedural movement is equivalent to professional environmental animation.


I want a substantial visual upgrade, not minor decorative changes.


Implement the improvements in stages, verify them in Preview, and report which effects and visual improvements are actually working.


Keep the existing action-adventure gameplay. I am using Zoria: Age of Shattering as an ENVIRONMENTAL VISUAL QUALITY REFERENCE, not asking you to copy its gameplay.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

I inspected the project and made **no changes**.

1. **Can it load GLB/GLTF?**  
   Yes. It uses Three.js r180, which supports GLB/GLTF through `GLTFLoader`. The project currently imports only Three.js core; a loader import and asset-loading path would need to be added.

2. **Can we import professionally modelled environment assets?**  
   Yes. Trees, rocks, plants, buildings and other props can be loaded as GLB/GLTF models. There are **no environment model or texture assets in the project currently**, so suitable assets would need to be sourced or created. Each asset should be checked for licensing, attribution, scale, orientation, materials and file size.

3. **Can we use detailed PBR textures and materials?**  
   Yes. Three.js and GLTF support PBR materials, including base color, normal, roughness, metallic and ambient-occlusion maps. The current scene already uses standard materials and a generated ground texture, but detailed asset texture maps are not present. Textures can add substantial download and memory cost, especially at mobile resolutions.

4. **Can we improve water, lighting and shadows?**  
   Yes. Custom water shading, environment reflections and improved lighting are possible. The current water is a translucent ribbon with simple moving glints—not a water shader. Directional lighting and shadows are already enabled, with a 1024×1024 shadow map. That provides a starting point, but more elaborate effects should be tested carefully for rendering cost and visual benefit.

5. **Can animated environmental assets be imported?**  
   Yes. GLTF animation clips can be played with Three.js `AnimationMixer`. There is already procedural wind movement in the game, but no imported animated environment assets or GLTF animation system. For mobile, it would be sensible to limit how many animated models run at once.

6. **Can this run smoothly on Android?**  
   Potentially, but it is **not verified** on Android. Performance will depend on device GPU, model complexity, texture sizes, visible object count, draw calls, shadows and shader cost. Instancing, LODs, compressed textures and a reduced-effects mobile setting can help. The present renderer caps pixel ratio at 1.5, which is a useful existing safeguard, but it does not guarantee a frame rate.

7. **Best way to replace the procedural scenery without breaking the game**  
   Use a gradual, hybrid replacement:
   - Keep the existing gameplay systems, map coordinates, paths, river, bridges, region definitions and collision logic intact.
   - First add a small set of professionally modelled trees, rocks and plants as **visual-only props**, while preserving the existing collision data and placement rules.
   - Replace scenery by region in bounded batches; instance repeated compatible models and use LOD or simpler distant representations.
   - Treat terrain separately. The current ground mesh and gameplay height/collision both rely on procedural terrain calculations. Initially, any upgraded terrain surface should conform to that existing height function; replacing the height data itself should wait until movement, collision and landmarks have been updated and tested against it.
   - Add more detailed materials and water effects after the asset pipeline is working, then tune shadows and lighting against actual assets.
   - Test loading, appearance, gameplay collision, frame rate and memory on desktop and representative Android devices at each stage.

**Bottom line:** The project’s Three.js foundation can support the upgrade, but professionally authored assets, a GLTF loading pipeline, and mobile performance validation are all still needed. The safest substantial change is to replace the visible scenery in stages while leaving gameplay geometry and collision untouched initially.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Implement a reusable GLB/GLTF environment asset pipeline in the existing Three.js r180 game and demonstrate a real external model loading and rendering in Preview.

## Requirements
- Add matching GLTFLoader support, reusable model loading/placement/scaling/management, PBR materials and textures, progress/error handling, and region/biome metadata.
- Preserve terrain, player, camera, movement, collision, and gameplay; keep procedural scenery and add the model without replacing the environment.
- Optimize for Android, explain exactly where future assets belong, and report actual Preview test results without using placeholder geometry as proof.

## Decisions
- Use a real, suitably licensed external Sketchfab GLB as the demonstration asset.
- Initial intended candidate was “Stylized Tree by Lowlypoly” (UID `96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`, 3.8 MB, 1,192 faces, LowlyPoly, CC Attribution), subject to download and inspection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing Three.js r180 project; environment is currently procedural, with no external model pipeline.
- Searched Sketchfab and visually reviewed a candidate contact sheet.
- Installed Pillow into `/tmp/opencode/python-packages` for the search tool.

### Active
- Integrate GLTFLoader and a reusable asset manager; load a real GLB additively, with placement metadata and loading progress/error display.
- Verify the integrated model visually in Preview and report confirmed results.

### Blocked
- The downloaded file is not the intended “Stylized Tree by Lowlypoly”; it is “Giant Low Poly Tree” (UID `acfd2b7f80894848b56c2ac8e7e59572`) despite selecting index 1. Its inspector report has 7 meshes/materials, no textures, 954 faces, and no extensions. Do not treat it as the chosen demonstration asset; download the intended model using the exact search result index from a fresh search.

## Next Move
1. Download “Stylized Tree by Lowlypoly” using the exact result index from the fresh search; retain its attribution sidecar and inspect its GLB metadata/materials.
2. Add the r180-matched GLTFLoader import and reusable environment asset manager with loading progress/errors, transforms, cache/cloning or instancing as appropriate, and biome/region assignment metadata.
3. Add the real GLB visibly as an additive demonstration while leaving gameplay and existing scenery intact.
4. Run checks, launch Preview, verify model rendering and loading status, and report only confirmed results.
5. Explain the exact asset location and GLB/GLTF relative-path conventions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene creation, environment building, and render loop; integrate the loader.
- `index.html`: Three.js r180 import map; add matching loader import.
- `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb`: Currently contains the unintended Giant Low Poly Tree; replace with the intended asset.
- `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb.attribution.json`: Attribution sidecar for the currently downloaded unintended model.
- `.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/scripts/download_model.py`: Sketchfab search/download tool.
- `.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs`: GLB inspection tool.

## Important Context
- Working tree files were untracked in the last observed `git status`; pipeline implementation has not started.
- Search command requires `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/opencode/python-packages`.
- Fresh exact-title search returned the intended model at index `0`; previous combined-query index `1` referred to a different candidate, causing the incorrect download.
- Current unintended GLB inspector output: 77,008 bytes, 7 meshes, 7 materials, 0 textures, 954 faces, no extensions.
- No loader integration, Preview launch, or rendering result has been confirmed.

## Objective
- Implement a reusable GLB/GLTF environment asset pipeline in the existing Three.js r180 game and demonstrate a real external model loading and rendering in Preview.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing terrain, player, camera, movement, collision, gameplay, and procedural scenery; add the model additively.
- Include loading progress and error handling, reusable placement/scaling/management, PBR materials/textures, and biome/region metadata.
- Optimize for Android, explain where future assets belong and how paths work, and report actual Preview test results.

## Decisions
- Use “Stylized Tree by Lowlypoly” (UID `96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`, CC Attribution) as the external demonstration asset.
- Keep the asset and attribution sidecar at `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb` and `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb.attribution.json`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Downloaded the intended Sketchfab model; inspection confirms 1,192 faces, two embedded textures, and two PBR materials.
- Added `EnvironmentAssetManager` in `environment-assets.js` with cached loading, progress/error callbacks, model normalization, placement, and region/biome metadata.
- Added the matching Three.js r180 GLTFLoader import map and asset status UI.
- Added two additive Verdant Reach tree placements in `game.js`; procedural scenery and gameplay code remain in place.
- `node --check game.js` and `node --check environment-assets.js` passed.

### Active
- Validate Preview rendering/loading behavior, then report actual results and the exact asset/path conventions.

### Blocked
- No known blockers.

## Next Move
1. Open the running Preview and confirm the model loads, renders visibly, and reports status; inspect browser errors and correct any integration issues.
2. Run any relevant project checks and report only confirmed results.
3. Explain that future assets belong under `public/assets/environment/`; current GLB loading uses `./public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb`, while external `.gltf` files should use paths relative to their referencing document.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, asset manager integration, and demonstration placements.
- `environment-assets.js`: reusable GLTF loading and placement manager.
- `index.html`: Three.js r180 import map and asset status UI.
- `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb`: demonstration model.
- `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb.attribution.json`: attribution and asset metadata.
- `.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs`: GLB inspection tool.

## Important Context
- GLB inspection: 1,416,128 bytes, 2 meshes, 2 materials, 2 embedded textures, no animations or required extensions.
- Attribution identifies author LowlyPoly and CC Attribution; model URL is `https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/none-96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed project files, `public/`, and search contact-sheet outputs as untracked.

## Environment models

Place environment `.glb` and `.gltf` assets under `public/assets/environment/`; keep attribution and license details alongside each model (the demo uses `stylized-tree.glb.attribution.json`). The demo asset is **Stylized Tree by Lowlypoly**, used under **CC Attribution**; see [its attribution record](public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb.attribution.json) and [Sketchfab page](https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/none-96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710).

`game.js` creates an `EnvironmentAssetManager` from `environment-assets.js` and calls `place(url, placements, options)`. Placements carry a world position, optional rotation/scale, and region/biome labels. Models are cached by ID, normalized to the requested height, and shared across placed instances. Status callbacks cover loading progress, success, and errors.

For this app served from its project root, the demo uses `./public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb`. Keep a standalone GLB path relative to the page URL. For a `.gltf`, upload its referenced textures and buffers beside it in the same relative folder structure: GLTFLoader resolves those dependency paths relative to the `.gltf` document.

I want a major visual upgrade to BOTH the ground/terrain and the vegetation of the existing 3D fantasy RPG.

The newly imported GLB tree model looks better than the old procedural trees. Now I want to expand its use throughout the world and improve the ground to match its quality.


1. Replace the old trees


- Use the newly imported GLB tree model as the starting point.
- Replace the basic procedural trees throughout the existing world with detailed imported 3D tree models.
- Add several different tree variations, sizes and shapes to avoid repetition.
- Use suitable additional professionally modelled tree assets if available.
- Preserve natural tree placement and existing collision boundaries.
- Use efficient instancing or other appropriate optimization methods.


2. Upgrade the ground


- Replace the basic green ground appearance with detailed PBR terrain materials.
- Add natural grass, soil, moss, dirt, fallen leaves and small stones.
- Create realistic transitions between different ground materials.
- Add winding dirt paths through forests and around villages.
- Improve terrain surface detail without changing existing terrain height or gameplay geometry.


3. Improve environmental vegetation


- Add detailed bushes, shrubs, plants, flowers and ground vegetation.
- Use imported 3D assets where appropriate.
- Make vegetation density and variety feel natural.
- Avoid repetitive arrangements.


4. Visual consistency


- Make the ground, trees and vegetation feel like parts of one professionally designed fantasy RPG environment.
- Improve material quality, lighting and environmental shadows where practical.
- Avoid the basic idle-game appearance.


5. Technical requirements


- Preserve existing player, movement, camera, terrain height, collision and gameplay.
- Keep Android performance in mind.
- Use LODs, instancing and compressed textures where appropriate.
- Do not remove working GLB loading functionality.


IMPORTANT:
Do not merely change colours or add a few decorations. Make a substantial visual improvement.


Inspect the existing assets and terrain system first. Implement the upgrade in stages and verify the actual result in Preview.


Report which old trees were replaced, which new assets were added, and what changed in the ground materials.
