<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Substantially upgrade the fantasy RPG’s ground, trees, and vegetation while preserving gameplay and verifying the result in Preview.

## Requirements
- Inspect terrain and assets before implementing; make a substantial, staged visual overhaul and verify it in Preview.
- Replace procedural trees with varied detailed imported models while preserving placements and collision boundaries; optimize for Android.
- Upgrade ground materials and transitions with grass, soil, moss, dirt, leaves, and stones, plus winding paths, without changing terrain height or gameplay geometry.
- Add naturally arranged bushes, shrubs, plants, flowers, and ground vegetation; improve visual consistency, lighting, and practical shadows.
- Preserve the player, movement, camera, collisions, gameplay, and working GLB loading.
- Report which old trees were replaced, new assets added, and ground material changes.

## Decisions
- Store environment assets under `public/assets/environment/` and keep attribution sidecars.
- Existing imported tree is “Stylized Tree by Lowlypoly” (UID `96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`, CC Attribution).

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected terrain generation, ground texture, paths, tree placement/collision code, vegetation, lighting, and GLTF manager in `game.js` and `environment-assets.js`.
- Confirmed the existing imported tree is additive at two Verdant Reach placements; procedural trees populate all regions.
- Reviewed candidate tree metadata; candidates include several low-poly trees, but none has been selected, downloaded, or integrated.

### Active
- Select visually suitable, downloadable tree models, inspect them, and preserve their attribution sidecars.
- Replace procedural tree populations while preserving placements and collision radii.
- Substantially improve ground materials and path transitions without changing terrain geometry.
- Enhance natural vegetation variety and density.
- Verify appearance, asset loading, and browser errors in Preview; report actual changes and verification results.

### Blocked
- Downloader help command fails because Python Pillow is unavailable: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL'`. The candidate image was read, but its visual content was not available in the tool result; model selection remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Inspect candidate visuals through an alternate supported method or resolve Pillow, then select and download suitable models with attribution.
2. Implement tree, ground, and vegetation upgrades in stages while preserving terrain height, path network, collision boundaries, and gameplay.
3. Run syntax and diff checks, inspect the application in Preview, and fix loading or visual issues.
4. Report replaced trees, added assets and attributions, ground material changes, and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: terrain, ground texture, paths, procedural trees, vegetation, collisions, and current GLTF placements.
- `environment-assets.js`: reusable GLTF loading, normalization, caching, placement, and status reporting.
- `index.html`: Three.js import map and asset status UI.
- `public/assets/environment/`: current imported tree asset and future environment assets.
- `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb.attribution.json`: attribution and model metadata.
- `.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/scripts/download_model.py`: model search/download utility.
- `/tmp/opencode/tree-overhaul-candidates.json`: recent Sketchfab candidate metadata.
- `/tmp/opencode/tree-overhaul-candidates.png`: candidate contact sheet.
- `sketchfab-preview-sheet.json`: existing imported tree metadata.
- `README.md`: environment asset paths and loader notes.

## Important Context
- Existing model: `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb`, 1,416,128 bytes; attribution records 1,192 faces, 1,030 vertices, 2 textures, and no animations.
- CC Attribution candidates include “Low Poly Pine” by Afloat Above the World (UID `107e3eab9dcb4e29a282c6709178752f`) and “Stylized Pine Tree Tree” by Batuhan13 (UID `deadcadc915545a7b4701dbe6eb419e8`); neither has been visually selected.
- `buildTreesAndRocks()` creates 28 procedural trees per region and adds trunk-based collision radii; tree canopy is walk-through.
- Existing path network, terrain dimensions, and height generation are in `game.js`; preserve them.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files already contain user/project changes.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Substantially upgrade the fantasy RPG’s ground, trees, and vegetation while preserving gameplay and verifying the result in Preview.

## Requirements
- Inspect terrain and assets before implementing; make a substantial, staged visual overhaul and verify it in Preview.
- Replace procedural trees with varied detailed imported models while preserving placements and collision boundaries; optimize for Android.
- Upgrade ground materials and transitions with grass, soil, moss, dirt, leaves, and stones, plus winding paths, without changing terrain height or gameplay geometry.
- Add naturally arranged bushes, shrubs, plants, flowers, and ground vegetation; improve visual consistency, lighting, and practical shadows.
- Preserve the player, movement, camera, collisions, gameplay, and working GLB loading.
- Report which old trees were replaced, new assets added, and ground material changes.

## Decisions
- Store environment assets under `public/assets/environment/` and keep attribution sidecars.
- Existing imported tree is “Stylized Tree by Lowlypoly” (UID `96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`, CC Attribution).

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected terrain generation, ground texture, paths, tree placement/collision code, vegetation, lighting, and GLTF manager in `game.js` and `environment-assets.js`.
- Confirmed the existing imported tree is additive at two Verdant Reach placements; procedural trees populate all regions.
- Reviewed candidate tree metadata, including CC Attribution candidates “Low Poly Pine” by Afloat Above the World (UID `107e3eab9dcb4e29a282c6709178752f`) and “Stylized Pine Tree Tree” by Batuhan13 (UID `deadcadc915545a7b4701dbe6eb419e8`).
- Read the candidate contact sheet file, but its visual content was not available for assessment.

### Active
- Select visually suitable, downloadable tree models, inspect them, and preserve their attribution sidecars.
- Replace procedural tree populations while preserving placements and collision radii.
- Substantially improve ground materials and path transitions without changing terrain geometry.
- Enhance natural vegetation variety and density.
- Verify appearance, asset loading, and browser errors in Preview; report actual changes and verification.

### Blocked
- The model search/download utility cannot run because Python Pillow is unavailable; even `--help` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL'`. Candidate model selection remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Inspect candidate visuals through an alternate supported method or resolve Pillow, then select and download suitable models with attribution.
2. Implement tree, ground, and vegetation upgrades in stages while preserving terrain height, path network, collision boundaries, and gameplay.
3. Run syntax and diff checks, inspect the application in Preview, and fix loading or visual issues.
4. Report replaced trees, added assets and attributions, ground material changes, and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: terrain, ground texture, paths, procedural trees, vegetation, collisions, lighting, and current GLTF placements.
- `environment-assets.js`: reusable GLTF loading, normalization, caching, placement, and status reporting.
- `public/assets/environment/`: current imported tree asset and future environment assets.
- `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb.attribution.json`: attribution and model metadata.
- `.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/scripts/download_model.py`: model search/download utility; currently blocked by Pillow.
- `/tmp/opencode/tree-overhaul-candidates.json`: candidate model metadata.
- `/tmp/opencode/tree-overhaul-candidates.png`: candidate contact sheet.
- `sketchfab-preview-sheet.json`: existing imported tree metadata.
- `README.md`: environment asset paths and loader notes.

## Important Context
- Existing model: `public/assets/environment/stylized-tree.glb`, 1,416,128 bytes; attribution records 1,192 faces, 1,030 vertices, 2 textures, and no animations.
- `buildTreesAndRocks()` generates 28 procedural tree candidates per region and adds trunk-based collision radii; canopies are walk-through.
- Existing path network, terrain dimensions, and height generation are in `game.js`; preserve them.
- Project changes are uncommitted; project files already contain user/project changes.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Substantially upgrade the fantasy RPG’s ground, trees, and vegetation while preserving gameplay and verifying the result in Preview.

## Requirements
- Inspect terrain and assets before implementing; make a substantial, staged visual overhaul and verify it in Preview.
- Replace procedural trees with varied detailed imported models while preserving placements and collision boundaries; optimize for Android.

## Objective
- Substantially upgrade the fantasy RPG’s ground, trees, and vegetation while preserving gameplay and verifying the result in Preview.

## Requirements
- Inspect terrain and assets before implementing; make a substantial, staged visual overhaul and verify it in Preview.
- Replace procedural trees with varied detailed imported models while preserving placements and collision boundaries; optimize for Android.
- Upgrade ground materials and transitions with grass, soil, moss, dirt, leaves, and stones, plus winding paths, without changing terrain height or gameplay geometry.
- Add naturally arranged bushes, shrubs, plants, flowers, and ground vegetation; improve visual consistency, lighting, and practical shadows.
- Preserve the player, movement, camera, collisions, gameplay, and working GLB loading.
- Report which old trees were replaced, new assets added, and ground material changes.

## Decisions
- Store environment assets under `public/assets/environment/` and keep attribution sidecars.
- Keep terrain geometry, path network, tree placements, and collision boundaries unchanged.
- Use the existing `EnvironmentAssetManager` for imported GLB loading and placement.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected terrain generation, ground texture, paths, tree placement/collision code, vegetation, lighting, and GLTF manager in `game.js` and `environment-assets.js`.
- Resolved the downloader’s Pillow dependency by installing Pillow.
- Added two downloaded Sketchfab GLBs and attribution sidecars: `broadleaf-tree.glb` (UID `4475c38dac544c8abe49ffa602df6595`) and `low-poly-pine.glb` (UID `107e3eab9dcb4e29a282c6709178752f`).
- Inspected both GLBs; they contain embedded textures and no animations.

### Active
- Replace procedural tree populations with varied imported models while preserving placement and trunk collision radii.
- Upgrade ground materials and paths without changing terrain geometry or gameplay.
- Improve vegetation variety/density and lighting/shadows.
- Verify appearance, asset loading, and browser errors in Preview; report actual changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect model appearance and suitability, then integrate the imported trees into the existing generated tree placements.
2. Upgrade the ground texture and path transitions and add natural vegetation detail while preserving terrain height and gameplay.
3. Run syntax and diff checks, inspect the application in Preview, and fix loading or visual issues.
4. Report replaced trees, added assets and attributions, ground material changes, and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: terrain, ground, paths, procedural trees, vegetation, collisions, lighting, and imported tree placements.
- `environment-assets.js`: reusable GLTF loading, normalization, caching, placement, and status reporting.
- `public/assets/environment/`: existing and newly added environment models and attribution sidecars.
- `public/assets/environment/broadleaf-tree.glb.attribution.json`: attribution for the broadleaf tree (CC Attribution).
- `public/assets/environment/low-poly-pine.glb.attribution.json`: attribution for the low-poly pine (CC Attribution).
- `README.md`: environment asset paths and loader notes.
- `/tmp/opencode/tree-overhaul-candidates.json`: candidate model metadata.
- `/tmp/opencode/tree-overhaul-candidates.png`: candidate contact sheet.

## Important Context
- Current procedural trees are created in `buildTreesAndRocks()`; it generates 28 candidates per region and adds trunk-based collision radii, while canopies are walk-through.
- Existing imported “Stylized Tree by Lowlypoly” (UID `96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`, CC Attribution) remains placed at two Verdant Reach locations; no tree replacement or ground/vegetation overhaul has yet been implemented.
- New broadleaf model is 2.17 MB; new low-poly pine model is 842 KB. Both use the public Sketchfab viewer extraction workflow.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Overhaul the fantasy RPG’s ground, trees, and vegetation while preserving gameplay, then verify the result in Preview.

## Requirements
- Inspect terrain and assets before implementing; make a substantial, staged visual overhaul and verify it in Preview.
- Replace procedural trees with varied detailed imported models while preserving placements and collision boundaries; optimize for Android.
- Upgrade ground materials and transitions with grass, soil, moss, dirt, leaves, and stones, plus winding paths, without changing terrain height or gameplay geometry.
- Add naturally arranged bushes, shrubs, plants, flowers, and ground vegetation; improve visual consistency, lighting, and practical shadows.
- Preserve the player, movement, camera, collisions, gameplay, and working GLB loading.
- Report which old trees were replaced, new assets added, and ground material changes.

## Decisions
- Store environment assets under `public/assets/environment/` and keep attribution sidecars.
- Keep terrain geometry, path network, tree placements, and collision boundaries unchanged.
- Use the existing `EnvironmentAssetManager` for imported GLB loading and placement.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected terrain generation, ground texture, paths, tree placement/collision code, vegetation, lighting, and GLTF manager.
- Added `broadleaf-tree.glb` and `low-poly-pine.glb` with attribution sidecars; both have embedded textures and no animations.

### Active
- Replace procedural tree populations with varied imported models while preserving placements and trunk collision radii.
- Upgrade ground materials and paths without changing terrain geometry or gameplay.
- Improve vegetation variety/density and lighting/shadows.
- Verify appearance, asset loading, and browser errors in Preview; report actual changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Integrate the imported models into generated tree placements and preserve trunk collision radii.
2. Upgrade ground materials, path transitions, and natural vegetation without changing terrain height or gameplay.
3. Run syntax and diff checks; inspect the application in Preview and address loading or visual issues.
4. Report replaced trees, added assets and attributions, ground material changes, and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: terrain, ground, paths, procedural trees, vegetation, collisions, lighting, and imported tree placements.
- `environment-assets.js`: GLTF loading, normalization, caching, placement, and status reporting.
- `public/assets/environment/`: environment models and attribution sidecars.
- `public/assets/environment/broadleaf-tree.glb.attribution.json`: attribution for broadleaf tree UID `4475c38dac544c8abe49ffa602df6595`.
- `public/assets/environment/low-poly-pine.glb.attribution.json`: attribution for pine UID `107e3eab9dcb4e29a282c6709178752f`.
- `README.md`: environment asset paths and loader notes.
- `/tmp/opencode/tree-overhaul-candidates.json`: candidate model metadata.
- `/tmp/opencode/tree-overhaul-candidates.png`: candidate contact sheet.

## Important Context
- `buildTreesAndRocks()` currently generates 28 tree candidates per region and adds trunk-based collision radii; canopies are walk-through.
- Existing `stylized-tree.glb` (UID `96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`, CC Attribution) remains placed at two Verdant Reach locations.
- New broadleaf model is about 2.1 MB; pine model is about 823 KB.
- Changes are uncommitted; repository status showed `README.md` modified and project files/assets untracked.

## Objective
- Overhaul the fantasy RPG’s ground, trees, and vegetation while preserving gameplay, then verify the result in Preview.

## Requirements
- Inspect terrain and assets before implementing; make a substantial, staged visual overhaul and verify it in Preview.
- Replace procedural trees with varied detailed imported models while preserving placements and collision boundaries; optimize for Android.
- Upgrade ground materials and transitions with grass, soil, moss, dirt, leaves, and stones, plus winding paths, without changing terrain height or gameplay geometry.
- Add naturally arranged bushes, shrubs, plants, flowers, and ground vegetation; improve visual consistency, lighting, and practical shadows.
- Preserve the player, movement, camera, collisions, gameplay, and working GLB loading.
- Report which old trees were replaced, new assets added, and ground material changes.

## Decisions
- Store environment assets under `public/assets/environment/` and keep attribution sidecars.
- Keep terrain geometry, path network, tree placements, and collision boundaries unchanged.
- Use the existing `EnvironmentAssetManager` for imported GLB loading and placement.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected terrain generation, ground texture, paths, tree placement/collision code, vegetation, lighting, and GLTF manager.
- Added `broadleaf-tree.glb` and `low-poly-pine.glb` with attribution sidecars; both have embedded textures and no animations.
- Began replacing procedural trees: removed the shared procedural trunk and foliage geometry declarations in `game.js`.

### Active
- Integrate imported models into generated tree placements while preserving placements and trunk collision radii.
- Upgrade ground materials, path transitions, vegetation variety/density, lighting, and shadows without changing terrain height or gameplay.
- Run checks and verify appearance, asset loading, and browser errors in Preview; report actual changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Replace procedural tree rendering in `buildTreesAndRocks()` with varied imported models; preserve tree placement generation and collision radii.
2. Upgrade ground materials and natural vegetation without changing terrain geometry or gameplay.
3. Run syntax and diff checks; inspect the application in Preview and address loading or visual issues.
4. Report replaced trees, added assets and attributions, ground material changes, and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: terrain, ground, paths, procedural tree/vegetation generation, collisions, lighting, and imported tree placements.
- `environment-assets.js`: GLTF loading, normalization, caching, placement, and status reporting.
- `public/assets/environment/`: environment models and attribution sidecars.
- `public/assets/environment/broadleaf-tree.glb.attribution.json`: attribution for broadleaf tree UID `4475c38dac544c8abe49ffa602df6595`.

- Changes are uncommitted; earlier status showed `README.md` modified and project files/assets untracked.

## Objective
- Overhaul the fantasy RPG’s ground, trees, and vegetation while preserving gameplay, then verify the result in Preview.

## Requirements
- Inspect terrain and assets before implementing; make a substantial, staged visual overhaul and verify it in Preview.
- Replace procedural trees with varied detailed imported models while preserving placements and collision boundaries; optimize for Android.
- Upgrade ground materials and transitions with grass, soil, moss, dirt, leaves, and stones, plus winding paths, without changing terrain height or gameplay geometry.
- Add naturally arranged bushes, shrubs, plants, flowers, and ground vegetation; improve visual consistency, lighting, and practical shadows.
- Preserve the player, movement, camera, collisions, gameplay, and working GLB loading.
- Report which old trees were replaced, new assets added, and ground material changes.

## Decisions
- Store environment assets under `public/assets/environment/` and keep attribution sidecars.
- Keep terrain geometry, path network, tree placement generation, and collision boundaries unchanged.
- Use the existing `EnvironmentAssetManager` for imported GLB loading and placement.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected terrain generation, ground texture, paths, tree placement/collision code, vegetation, lighting, and GLTF manager.
- Added `broadleaf-tree.glb` and `low-poly-pine.glb` with attribution sidecars; both are textured and have no animations.
- Replaced generated procedural tree geometry with imported-model placements; retained deterministic placement logic and original trunk collision radius.
- Enabled shadow casting and receiving on imported tree meshes.
- Improved ground texture with moss/soil patches, fine grain, leaf-like flecks, and stone-colored specks; layered winding path ribbons soften path edges.
- Clustered ground-cover placement around deterministic biome patches and increased grass, flower, and shrub counts.
- Added README attribution notes for all three tree assets.
- Fixed the asset status callback to receive the model `id`; `node --check game.js`, `node --check environment-assets.js`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Confirmed GLB headers and metadata: broadleaf has 3 meshes/3 textures; pine has 2 meshes/2 textures; both are glTF 2.0 assets.

### Active
- Review final changes for visual, gameplay/collision, and Android performance regressions.
- Launch the game and verify tree loading, ground/path visuals, shadows, gameplay, and browser errors in Preview.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining changes and confirm no gameplay geometry, movement, or collision behavior was altered.
2. Launch the app and verify it in Preview; inspect the rendered scene and browser console.
3. Address any visual or loading regressions, then report replaced trees, added assets and attributions, material changes, and actual verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: terrain, ground texture, path ribbons, ground cover, tree placement, collisions, and asset setup.
- `environment-assets.js`: GLTF loading, normalization, caching, placement, and shadow flags.
- `public/assets/environment/`: imported tree GLBs and attribution sidecars.
- `README.md`: asset attribution and loader notes.
- `index.html`: game page, UI, and module import map.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `README.md` modified and project files/assets untracked.
- `buildTreesAndRocks()` generates 28 tree candidates per region and retains trunk-based collision radii; imported canopies remain walk-through.
- Existing `stylized-tree.glb` (UID `96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`, CC Attribution) remains placed at two Verdant Reach locations.
- New broadleaf: UID `4475c38dac544c8abe49ffa602df6595`, about 2.1 MB; pine: UID `107e3eab9dcb4e29a282c6709178752f`, about 823 KB.
- Preview verification has not yet been performed.

## Objective
- Overhaul the fantasy RPG’s ground, trees, and vegetation while preserving gameplay, then verify the result in Preview.

## Requirements
- Inspect terrain and assets before implementation; make a substantial visual overhaul and verify it in Preview.
- Replace procedural trees with varied detailed imported models while preserving placements and collision boundaries; optimize for Android.
- Upgrade ground materials and transitions with grass, soil, moss, dirt, leaves, and stones, plus winding paths, without changing terrain height or gameplay geometry.
- Add naturally arranged bushes, shrubs, plants, flowers, and ground vegetation; improve visual consistency, lighting, and practical shadows.
- Preserve the player, movement, camera, collisions, gameplay, and working GLB loading.
- Report which old trees were replaced, new assets added, and ground material changes.

## Decisions
- Store environment assets under `public/assets/environment/` and keep attribution sidecars.
- Keep terrain geometry, path network, tree placement generation, and collision boundaries unchanged.
- Use the existing `EnvironmentAssetManager` for imported GLB loading and placement.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected terrain generation, ground texture, paths, tree placement/collision code, vegetation, lighting, and GLTF manager.
- Added `broadleaf-tree.glb` and `low-poly-pine.glb` with attribution sidecars; both are textured and static.
- Replaced generated procedural tree geometry with imported-model placements; retained deterministic placement logic and original trunk collision radius.
- Enabled shadow casting and receiving on imported tree meshes.
- Improved ground texture with moss/soil patches, fine grain, leaf-like flecks, and stone-colored specks; layered winding path ribbons soften path edges.
- Clustered ground-cover placement around deterministic biome patches and increased grass, flower, and shrub counts.
- Added README attribution notes for all three tree assets; fixed the asset status callback to receive model `id`.
- Verified `node --check game.js`, `node --check environment-assets.js`, `git diff --check`, GLB headers/metadata, and Preview loading.
- Opened `http://localhost:3002/index.html`, started gameplay, confirmed WebGL canvas and no console errors; all three GLBs returned HTTP 200 and status reported the broadleaf ready. Captured `/tmp/opencode/environment-preview.png`.

### Active
- Review captured Preview image and finish visual/gameplay/performance regression assessment.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/environment-preview.png` for visual regressions; if needed, continue checking gameplay movement/collisions and Android performance.
2. Report replaced trees, added assets and attributions, material changes, and actual verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: terrain, ground texture, path ribbons, ground cover, tree placement, collisions, and asset setup.
- `environment-assets.js`: GLTF loading, normalization, caching, placement, and shadow flags.
- `public/assets/environment/`: imported tree GLBs and attribution sidecars.
- `README.md`: asset attribution and loader notes.
- `/tmp/opencode/environment-preview.png`: Preview capture for visual inspection.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files/assets are untracked, and `README.md` is modified.
- `buildTreesAndRocks()` generates 28 tree candidates per region and retains trunk-based collision radii; imported canopies remain walk-through.
- Existing `stylized-tree.glb` (UID `96bfe5f5fe3e43e9b4db5ab78fd12710`, CC Attribution) remains at two original Verdant Reach placements.
- New broadleaf: UID `4475c38dac544c8abe49ffa602df6595`, about 2.1 MB; pine: UID `107e3eab9dcb4e29a282c6709178752f`, about 823 KB.
- Preview emitted GPU stall `ReadPixels` warnings under software rendering; there were no console errors.

metadata.displayText:
The new imported broadleaf and pine trees have significantly improved the visual quality of my game, but there is a serious performance problem.

When the player approaches areas containing many trees, the FPS drops dramatically and gameplay becomes laggy.


I want you to optimize the forest rendering without sacrificing the improved visual quality.


1. Investigate the actual bottleneck


Inspect the current Three.js renderer and environment asset system.
Determine whether the FPS drop is caused by:


- Too many draw calls.
- Too many visible tree meshes.
- Expensive GLB materials or textures.
- Excessive shadow rendering.
- Too many transparent materials.
- Excessive geometry or GPU memory usage.
- Inefficient object visibility management.


Profile dense forest areas instead of guessing.


2. Optimize tree rendering


- Use THREE.InstancedMesh wherever compatible.
- Reuse shared geometries and materials.
- Avoid creating duplicate materials or unnecessary objects.
- Implement frustum culling.
- Add distance-based LOD (Level of Detail).
- Use simplified tree models at greater distances.
- Hide or simplify trees that are too far away to be noticeable.
- Optimize shadows for trees, especially in dense forests.


3. Preserve visual quality


IMPORTANT:


- Do not replace the imported trees with the old procedural trees.
- Do not remove most of the forest.
- Do not make nearby trees look noticeably worse.
- Keep broadleaf and pine variations.
- Preserve natural tree placement and existing collision behavior.
- Maintain the improved ground and vegetation.


4. Android optimization
